title: Payload Surgeon: layered payload debugger and error taxonomy for Console
creator: Lina Chen
description: This ticket captures the UX design for 'Payload Surgeon' — a compact, multi-pane debugger inside the Redwood Console focused on failed requests, retry patterns, and an actionable error taxonomy. The goal is to let engineers and product owners triage a failed inference call quickly: see the timeline of attempts, inspect request/response payloads side-by-side, surface probable root causes via an error taxonomy, and offer one-click remedial actions (retry with tweak, rollback rollout, open a canary snapshot). The design must link to cost & rollout metadata so teams can reason about trade-offs when selecting fixes.
personas: ML Engineer: needs to reproduce failures and tweak KV/cache settings
SRE/Platform Engineer: needs to assess whether failures are infra or model-related
Product Manager: wants a quick summary to decide on rollbacks or mitigations
goals: Surface the most likely cause for a failed request within three clicks
Allow safe local replays with KV overrides and token limits without leaving Console
Make retry, rollback, and canary snapshot actions discoverable and low-friction
Correlate failure events with cost/latency spikes and rollout configuration
acceptance_criteria: Design mockups for desktop and narrow tablet demonstrating: timeline, attempt stack, payload diff panel, taxonomy ribbon, and quick action bar
Prototype (Figma) that shows a 3-step replay flow with KV override prefill and telemetry consent
List of required telemetry events and low-cardinality tags for engineering handoff
UX copy reviewed and signed off by PM and Legal for any user-triggered replay that may expose PII
Integration points mapped: Rollouts API, Cost Insights, Request Trace links
design_notes: Primary view is a horizontally-split canvas: left timeline of attempts, center payload diff (request/response), right taxonomy + suggested actions
Use a compact inline diff for request JSON with tokenized highlighting for long strings (collapsible) to avoid overwhelming the user
Taxonomy should be ranked by confidence and show evidence pointers (e.g., KV-cache-miss, OOM on host, model-timeout). Each taxonomy row links to related runbook nodes
Quick actions include: Replay (with sandbox override), Retry on upstream, Pin as false-positive, Create Incident with snapshot
Expose a cost delta preview when toggling replay variants (e.g., larger context window increases cost estimate)
Accessibility: keyboard-first navigation across attempts and actions; color-blind friendly palettes for taxonomy severities
decisions: Inline payload diffs chosen over full raw view by default to reduce cognitive load — raw payload accessible via a toggle
Default taxonomy ranking algorithm will combine signal weight from model logs, infra traces, and historical request fingerprints
Replays default to a read-only sandbox that strips customer PII unless explicit consent is granted by the user
open_questions: Should replay be limited by role (Console RBAC) or by project-level opt-in? (security trade-off)
How granular should suggested actions be for PMs vs engineers? (one-click rollback vs advanced replay config)
What is the expected retention window for snapshots used in payload diffs? Should it follow the general traces retention policy?
tasks: Finalize taxonomy seed set and map to evidence pointers — owner: Diego Morales
Engineering sync: list telemetry events and API hooks required — owner: Asha Patel
Prototype usability test with 6 engineers and 2 PMs (script + tasks) — owner: Lina Chen
Security review for replay sandbox and PII stripping behavior — owner: Priya Rao
Implement copy deck and microcopy for quick actions — owner: Marcus O'Neill
review_feedback: PM (Eleanor Wu): prefer the timeline to surface aggregate retry rates and a single-click ‘collapse repeats’ control
Eng (Omar Khalid): need explicit telemetry for 'replay_with_overrides' and a circuit breaker if replay rate spikes
SRE (Jill Martinez): flag low-cardinality fields in payloads to avoid indexing explosion — hide by default
Design (Ravi Singh): consider an unobtrusive mini-tutorial for first-time users of Payload Surgeon
next_steps: Run prototype usability sessions and capture task completion times
Deliver telemetry contract to engineering and confirm storage/retention constraints
Address feedback from PM and SRE; ship updated Figma frames for final sign-off
Coordinate with Console infra to expose rollout metadata API for quick rollback action
